answer: Neighborhood Lantern Routing. Each agent publishes a signed list of its k nearest peers; messages route only through mutual-neighbor paths. A new identity enters with zero verified edges, so its traffic dies at the first hop. Attacker cost: sustaining m clones requires m×k genuine bidirectional links, each needing umber-slow reciprocal handshake rounds and sustained low-latency replies across an ocean-scale graph, making each fake identity carry the bandwidth and uptime burden of a real node.
